skill.name: grimoire-polymarket
skill.description: Queries Polymarket market data and CLOB state, and manages CLOB orders through the Grimoire venue CLI wrapper.
skill.summary: Use Grimoire CLI workflows for Polymarket discovery, CLOB data, and authenticated order operations.
skill.author: franalgaba

security_audit.summary: The external-command alerts are mostly Markdown backtick false positives, but several Grimoire, npx, bun, and brew invocations are real command surfaces. The skill also requires Polymarket private keys or API credentials and supports authenticated order workflows, so users need strong warnings and confirmation controls. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Sensitive Polymarket credentials are required for authenticated workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to keep private keys and API credentials in environment storage only, and never paste them into prompts or logs.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends no-install package execution and local package installation commands.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a pinned, preinstalled CLI binary. Require user confirmation before npx, bun, brew, or package installation commands run.

remediation.issue: Authenticated order and cancellation operations can change user positions.
remediation.suggestion: Make read-only discovery the default and require explicit confirmation before any order placement or cancellation operation.

static_findings.snippet: Use this skill for Polymarket market discovery, CLOB market data, and order-management operations th
Legacy compatibility aliases are still supported (`market`, `book`, `midpoint`, `spread`, `price`, `
- optional signature routing: `POLYMARKET_SIGNATURE_TYPE` (`0` EOA, `1` POLY_PROXY, `2` GNOSIS_SAFE)
- Install: `brew tap Polymarket/polymarket-cli && brew install polymarket`
- Prefer `--format json` for agent and automation workflows.
- `search-markets` is the agent-oriented normalized discovery command; passthrough `markets search`

content.value_statement: Polymarket research often requires several CLI commands across market discovery, CLOB data, and authenticated reads. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused Grimoire CLI surface for those workflows.
actual_capabilities: Runs Grimoire Polymarket info and status checks through the venue adapter.
Searches markets by query, slug, event, category, sport, league, and status.
Retrieves CLOB book, midpoint, price, trades, orders, and balance information.
Uses the official Polymarket CLI through a restricted wrapper surface.
Documents authenticated order and cancellation operation names for supported custom flows.
limitations: Requires the Grimoire CLI or official Polymarket CLI to be installed.
Authenticated operations require private key or API credentials in environment variables.
It does not provide investment advice or predict market outcomes.
It does not expose blocked wallet, bridge, approve, setup, upgrade, or shell groups.

use_cases.title: Research Active Markets
use_cases.description: Find open Polymarket markets by topic, event, category, sport, or league before deeper analysis.

use_cases.title: Inspect CLOB Liquidity
use_cases.description: Review books, midpoints, spreads, prices, trades, and balances for a known token or condition.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Route Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through the same Grimoire Polymarket command surface.

prompt_templates.title: Find Topic Markets
prompt_templates.prompt: Find active open Polymarket markets about bitcoin. Summarize the top results with status, event names, and end dates.

prompt_templates.title: Check CLOB Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the order book, midpoint, and price for token id <token_id>. Explain liquidity and any missing data.

prompt_templates.title: Compare League Markets
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare open and active sports markets for league <league>. Highlight tradable markets and key differences across events.

prompt_templates.title: Review Open Orders
prompt_templates.prompt: Using my configured environment credentials, inspect my open orders for market <condition_id>. Do not place or cancel orders without confirmation.

output_examples.output: A concise list of matching open markets, their slugs, event names, status, end dates, and follow-up identifiers.

output_examples.input: Inspect CLOB data for a token id.
output_examples.output: A short liquidity summary covering book depth, midpoint, current price, recent trades, and missing fields.

output_examples.input: Review my open orders for a market.
output_examples.output: A confirmation-safe account summary that lists open order status and avoids changes until the user approves them.

best_practices: Use read-only market discovery before any authenticated order workflow.
Store Polymarket credentials in environment variables, not in prompts or shared logs.
Request explicit user confirmation before any order placement or cancellation.
anti_patterns: Pasting private keys or API secrets into chat messages.
Running no-install package commands without checking the package source and version.
Treating market summaries as financial or betting advice.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides agents through Grimoire CLI commands for Polymarket discovery, CLOB data, and authenticated order workflows.

faq.question: Does it need credentials?
faq.answer: Read-only discovery may not need credentials. Authenticated CLOB operations require Polymarket private key or API credentials in environment variables.

faq.question: Can it place orders?
faq.answer: The documented adapter supports order and cancellation operations. Users should require explicit confirmation before any order changes.

faq.question: Which AI tools support it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it call Polymarket APIs directly?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs agents to use the Grimoire venue wrapper and the official Polymarket CLI backend.

faq.question: Is it safe for read-only research?
faq.answer: It can support read-only research, but users should verify commands and avoid exposing credentials in prompts or logs.
